'''Caroline Mary Series''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FRS}} (born 24 March 1951<ref name=whoswho/>) is an English mathematician known for her work in [[hyperbolic geometry]], [[Kleinian group]]s and [[dynamical systems]].

==Early life and education==
[[File:Caroline Series.jpg|thumb|right|Caroline in 1976]]
Series was born on March 24, 1951, in [[Oxford]] to Annette and [[George Series]].<ref name=whoswho/> She attended [[Oxford High School for Girls]] and from 1969 studied at [[Somerville College, Oxford]], where she was interviewed for admission by [[Anne Cobbe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://europeanwomeninmaths.org/sites/default/files/documents/portraits/ima_-mathematics-today.pdf|title=Interview with Professor Caroline Series|date=2007|website=European Women in Maths|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215727/http://europeanwomeninmaths.org/sites/default/files/documents/portraits/ima_-mathematics-today.pdf|archive-date=3 March 2016|url-status=dead|access-date=28 August 2018|df=dmy-all}}</ref> She obtained a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in Mathematics in 1972 and was awarded the university Mathematical Prize. She was awarded a [[Kennedy Scholarship]] and studied at [[Harvard University]] from 1972, obtaining her [[Ph.D.]] in 1976<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Caroline Mary|last=Series |title=Ergodic actions of product groups |publisher=Harvard University |date=1976 |url=http://id.lib.harvard.edu/aleph/003941242/catalog |oclc=76998584}}</ref> supervised by [[George Mackey]] on the ''[[Ergodicity]] of product groups''.<ref name=phd/><ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy|id=75406}}</ref>

==Career and research==
In 1976–77 she was a [[lecturer]] at [[University of California, Berkeley]], and in 1977–78 she was a [[research fellow]] at [[Newnham College, Cambridge]]. From 1978 she was at the [[University of Warwick]], first as a lecturer, then, from 1987, as a [[reader (academic rank)|reader]], and from 1992 as a professor. From 1999 to 2004 she was [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] (EPSRC) Senior Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

In the 1970s, Series found illustrations of [[Rufus Bowen]]'s Theory of Dynamic Systems in the geometry of [[continued fraction]]s and two-dimensional hyperbolic geometry, effect of [[Fuchsian group]]s. After that she investigated similar, including fractal, geometric patterns in three-dimensional hyperbolic spaces, with [[Kleinian group]]s  as [[symmetry group]]s. The computer images led to a book project with [[David Mumford]] and David Wright, which took over ten years. Other coauthors with whom she published in this area include [[Linda Keen]] and [[Joan Birman]].

Series became the third woman to be president of the [[London Mathematical Society]] when she held the post in 2017–2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Female Presidents for Three Maths Societies |url=https://ima.org.uk/8604/female-presidents-three-maths-societies/ |website=IMA |publisher=[[Institute of Mathematics]] |access-date=14 March 2021 |date=5 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=THE JEREMIAH HORROCKS LECTURE- Indra's Pearls: A mathematical adventure – CANCELLED |url=https://www.star.uclan.ac.uk/2020/02/19/the-jeremiah-horrocks-lecture-indras-pearls-a-mathematical-adventure/ |publisher=[[University of Central Lancashire]] |access-date=14 March 2021 |date=19 February 2020}}</ref>

She is emeritus professor in mathematics at the University of Warwick.<ref name=whoswho/>

===Honours and awards===
In 1987 she was awarded the Junior [[Whitehead Prize]] by the [[London Mathematical Society]]. In 1992 she held the Rouse Ball Lecture in Cambridge, and in 1986 she was the [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berkeley (''Symbolic Dynamics for Geodesic Flows''). From 1990 to 2001 she was the editor of the Student Texts of the London Mathematical Society. In 1986 she was a founding member of [[European Women in Mathematics]] (EWM).<ref>[http://europeanwomeninmaths.org/sites/default/files/documents/portraits/ima_-mathematics-today.pdf Interview] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215727/http://europeanwomeninmaths.org/sites/default/files/documents/portraits/ima_-mathematics-today.pdf# |date=3 March 2016 }} (PDF; 266&nbsp;kB)</ref> In 2009 she was the Emmy Noether visiting professor at the [[University of Göttingen]]. She was elected  a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in its inaugural class of 2013. She is an Honorary Fellow of Somerville College.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.some.ox.ac.uk/about-somerville/emeritus-and-honorary-fellows/|title=Emeritus and Honorary Fellows|access-date=26 August 2018|publisher=[[Somerville College, Oxford]]}}</ref>
*1972–74 Kennedy Scholarship, Harvard University 
*1987 Junior Whitehead Prize, London Mathematical Society  <ref name="List of LMS prize winners">{{cite web |url= http://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners |title= List of LMS prize winners|publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]]|access-date=8 September 2014}}</ref>
*2014 [[Senior Anne Bennett Prize]], London Mathematical Society <ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/lms-prizes-2014 |title=LMS Prizes 2014 |publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]]|access-date=8 September 2014}}</ref><ref name="List of LMS prize winners"/>
*2016 [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160429121459/https://royalsociety.org/people/caroline-series-12895|archive-date=29 April 2016|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/caroline-series-12895|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|title=Professor Caroline Series FRS|year=2016|website=royalsociety.org|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |date=September 25, 2015 |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies }}}}</ref>
*2017 Elected to the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{citation|title=List of members|publisher=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members|access-date=2020-10-02}}</ref>
*2021 [[David Crighton Medal]], London Mathematical Society<ref>{{cite journal|title=David Crighton Medal|journal=London Mathematical Society (LMS) Newsletter|issue=504|date=January 2023|page=10|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/inline-files/NLMS_504_for%20web.pdf}}</ref>

Series was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2023 Birthday Honours]] for services to mathematics.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=64082|supp=y|page=B10|date=17 June 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She is the daughter of the physicist [[George Series]].<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who  |title=Series, Prof. Caroline Mary | id = U287925 | year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.287925 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford }}</ref>
